response.sql: WITH team_avg AS (SELECT team_id, AVG(CAST(l AS REAL) / g) AS avg_loss_rate FROM manager_half WHERE g >= 53 AND l IS NOT NULL GROUP BY team_id) SELECT AVG(avg_loss_rate) AS avg_of_team_avgs FROM team_avg;

assumptions.assumption: Teams are identified by team_id across all years and leagues, so each team_id forms one group.
Each manager_half row is one observation, so the g >= 53 filter applies per row and each qualifying row counts equally in its team's average.
Rows with NULL l are excluded; AVG ignores NULL ratios, and g >= 53 already excludes NULL and zero g values.
The SQL dialect is SQLite-like, where CAST(l AS REAL) avoids integer truncation and CTEs are supported.

alternatives.interpretation: Group teams by franchise_id instead of team_id, so relocated or renamed franchises are combined. This requires joining manager_half to the team table on year, team_id, and league_id to get franchise_id.
alternatives.sql: WITH team_avg AS (SELECT t.franchise_id, AVG(CAST(m.l AS REAL) / m.g) AS avg_loss_rate FROM manager_half m JOIN team t ON t.team_id = m.team_id AND t.year = m.year AND t.league_id = m.league_id WHERE m.g >= 53 AND m.l IS NOT NULL GROUP BY t.franchise_id) SELECT AVG(avg_loss_rate) AS avg_of_team_avgs FROM team_avg;
